notes.text: Big suitcases leave for Kujō House (Osaka) by TA-Q-BIN this morning. Keep only an overnight bag each for Hakone tomorrow.
NOAH at Korakuen Hall is NOT confirmed until tickets are bought for all 8. No show or no tickets? Go straight to Kabukichō Tower instead.
Shorts or roll-up trousers for teamLab, passports for tonight, and cash for Golden Gai seat charges. Cold, dark early, and Odaiba is windy.

stops.summary: Ship the big suitcases to Osaka now, so Hakone is overnight bags only.
stops.story: This is the boring errand that makes the next three days easy: your suitcases vanish today and turn up at Kujō House on Monday evening. Nobody drags a suitcase onto the Romancecar.
how: Pack an overnight bag for Hakone, Odawara and the trip to Kyoto, then close up the suitcases.
Send them by Yamato TA-Q-BIN from the front desk or the nearest konbini to Kujō House, Mon 21 Dec evening delivery.
Leave for Higashi-Nagasaki for the 08:52 Seibu train to Ikebukuro.
tips: Photograph every waybill: it's your tracking number if a bag goes missing.
Keep passports, chargers and swimwear for the Hakone baths out of the suitcases.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Barefoot, knee-deep in glowing water, with flowers floating overhead. Book the 10:00 slot online only.
stops.story: teamLab Planets is a warehouse of digital art you wade through barefoot: the water rooms glow and ripple, and in the floating flower garden the flowers hang in the air around you. It's ridiculous, and the photos come out great.
how: Booked 10:00 slot for 8: tickets are online only, no door sales.
Shoes off at the lockers, roll trousers above the knee.
Do the water rooms first, then the floating flower garden.
tips: Shorts make it painless. Wet jeans in December don't.
Prices change by day and earlier booking is cheaper. Compare Klook with the official site, but Klook is usually non-refundable.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Glühwein by the water at the new Shin-Toyosu Christmas market: a light lunch with a souvenir mug.
stops.story: The Tokyo Christmas Market moved to a new waterfront site at Shin-Toyosu for 2026: German stalls, sausages, pretzels and steaming glühwein a couple of minutes from teamLab. In December it actually feels like a Christmas market, cold enough that the hot wine makes sense.
how: Walk 8 minutes from teamLab.
Show your KKday advance ticket (comes with the mug).
Sausages, pretzels and glühwein: keep it light, the baths are next.
tips: At busy times entry can be limited to advance ticket holders, so buy on KKday ahead of time.
Weekday entry is ¥1,000; weekends go up to ¥1,500.
stops.cost: ¥1,000 pp entry, plus food and drinks

stops.summary: Real Hakone spring water in the middle of Tokyo, and a rooftop foot bath with a view over the bay.
stops.story: Manyo Club trucks in hot-spring water from Hakone and Yugawara, so this is a proper onsen in the middle of the city. Yukata, towels, baths split by gender, and a rooftop foot-bath deck where all 8 of you can sit together looking over Tokyo Bay.
how: Walk 7 minutes from the market. Pay the set at the desk (bath, yukata, towels).
Baths split by gender. Meet back up on the mixed rooftop foot-bath deck.
Leave by 14:56 for the Yurikamome from Shijo-mae to Daiba.
tips: Anyone with tattoos is refused, even small ones or stickers. Check before you go.
Shower before you get in, and no swimsuits in the bath. Small towel on your head, not in the water.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: A 150 m fountain show set to music off Odaiba Seaside Park. Free, quick, and cancelled if it's windy.
stops.story: Tokyo Aqua Symphony shoots water across the bay to music in front of the Rainbow Bridge. It's a short show and a cheap win between the baths and dinner. Fair warning: the Unicorn Gundam at DiverCity is gone, so don't go looking.
how: Yurikamome to Daiba, then walk to Odaiba Seaside Park.
Catch the next show after 15:15. Shows run from about 15:00 and last about 10 min each.
Leave for the 16:08 Rinkai line from Tokyo Teleport toward Shinjuku.
tips: CHECK the schedule that morning: wind cancels shows and the start time sometimes moves.
Damp hair from the baths plus December wind off the bay is a bad combination. Dry it properly at Manyo.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Tokyo's benchmark tsukemen: be in the queue by 16:40, buy a ticket from the machine, eat in waves.
stops.story: Fuunji's thick noodles get dunked in a dense, almost gravy-like chicken-and-fish broth, and it's one of the few famous Shinjuku ramen queues that is actually worth it. The counter is small, so you'll go in waves.
how: Rinkai line to Osaki, Saikyo rapid to Shinjuku, then walk from the South Exit. Be in line by 16:40.
Buy tickets at the machine: tsukemen ¥1,000, or tokusei tsukemen ¥1,300 with everything on it.
Eat in waves at the counter. Leave by 18:07 for Suidobashi.
tips: No reservations, and service ends early when the soup sells out, so the 16:40 arrival is non-negotiable.
Ask for soup-wari at the end: they top up your dipping broth so you can drink it.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: NOAH at Korakuen Hall, the holy land of Japanese wrestling. CHECK tickets; fallback is Kabukichō Tower.
stops.story: Korakuen Hall is a small, steep, beat-up hall where every seat is close enough to hear the chops land, and wrestling fans call it the holy land. NOAH's year-end Thanksgiving show there is the kind of night you'll still be quoting on the flight home.
how: CHECK: watch noah.co.jp/schedule and e+ from mid-November and buy 8 seats together.
Bell is 18:30. You get to Suidobashi at 18:22 from Fuunji, so don't linger over the noodles.
Leaving after: Chuo-Sobu local from Suidobashi to Shinjuku at 21:16 (¥210).
tips: If e+ rejects a foreign card, use Jasumo, an English-language ticket proxy.
Leftover tickets are sometimes sold at the 5F counter on the day. Worth a try if you missed out.
No show or no tickets: go straight to Shinjuku for Kabukichō Tower's yokocho hall and the namco arcade.
stops.booking: Unconfirmed: tickets expected mid-November on e+; buy 8 together
wishes: Pro wrestling: Pro Wrestling NOAH Thanksgiving 2026 at Korakuen Hall (Plan C had Fri 18 Dec)
Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing

stops.summary: Neon food hall with shared tables for 8: rounds and snacks, then the namco arcade upstairs.
stops.story: Kabuki Yokocho, on the 2nd floor of Kabukichō Tower, is a food hall dressed up as a neon festival street, loud and garish, with stalls of regional food and shared tables big enough for all 8. It's dinner number two and the warm-up for Golden Gai.
how: Take the escalator to the 2nd floor and claim a shared table.
Send people to different stalls and bring it all back to the table.
Then do a lap of the namco arcade upstairs before the 9-minute walk to Golden Gai.
tips: Kabukichō touts will offer bars and clubs on the street. Ignore them all, no nightclubs.
Carry passports: the drinking age is 20 and some places check.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
No nightclubs (a group rule from Plan C; ignore touts and bar invites in Kabukichō)

stops.summary: The original sugoi niboshi: brutally fishy sardine ramen up a steep staircase in Golden Gai.
stops.story: Ramen Nagi's Golden Gai shop is where the 'sugoi niboshi' sardine ramen started: a bitter, punchy broth you either love or never forget. It's 10 seats at an L-shaped counter up a narrow staircase, open all night.
how: Climb the stairs and buy tickets at the machine.
Half the group eats while the other half scouts the first bars, then swap.
tips: Expect a short line even late. The 10 seats fill fast.
The broth is intensely fishy. Order it anyway.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Friday in Golden Gai: tiny bars, two groups of four, and a karaoke bar to finish.
stops.story: Golden Gai is about 200 bars crammed into a few alleys, most so small that 8 people is a takeover. Albatross G has two floors that can actually fit you, and Champion is the karaoke bar where strangers cheer your worst song.
how: Split into two groups of four: most bars seat only 6–10.
Start at Albatross G, then finish together at Champion for karaoke.
Home by taxi: two cars, 20 min, about ¥4,500 per car.
tips: Seat charges are ¥500–1,500 and many bars are cash only. Check the sign on the door before you sit.
Some bars are regulars-only. If there's a sign, move on.
Tomorrow is a 09:00 start for Hakone, so know when to call it.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
